newsitem.title: ITALY: ENEL said to limit buying from private sector.
newsitem.headline: ENEL said to limit buying from private sector.

text.p: Italy's state-owned electricity utility ENEL is set to stop buying excess electricity supplies from the private sector from this morning, Milan-based financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported on Thursday.

The value of this excess production is put at around 500 billion lire ($282.1 million) per year for ENEL, and the move, which follows talks between ENEL and Italy's Energy Authority, will have a beneficial effect on ENEL's balance sheet, the paper added. An ENEL spokesman declined to comment on the report.

Il Sole 24 Ore said the move will not effect private electricity plants which are dedicated to producing electricity for ENEL. But those such as Edison and Sondel, part of the Falck group, will be affected as they sell their excess electricity supplies to the state-owned utility.
These two private groups account for around 70 percent of this type of excess electricity sold to ENEL, Il Sole said.
Edison shares were off 4.34 pct at 8,795 lire and Falck was down 2.34 pct at 6,650 at 0935 GMT in a firmer Milan market.

Edison has been critical of a move by ENEL to set up a joint electricity production venture with state-controlled oil giant ENI. Edison says this could create barriers to entry for other producers in the market.
Italy is planning the privatisation of ENEL, but there is no definite timetable at the moment.
